chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'None can revoke the marriage except the father.'
ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to revoke a marriage contract according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the exclusive authority of the father (or paternal grandfather) in dissolving a marriage contract, a key distinction in Shia fiqh that differentiates the wali's role from other guardians. It reflects the principle that the marriage bond, once established by the guardian's consent, can only be severed by that same authority, emphasizing the structural integrity of the family unit in early Shia legal thought.
